ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Ada Lovelace

code.originalText: Twenty-week review after the last chemotherapy cycle: blood counts, thyroid on pembrolizumab, tapering morphine, mood and her work

text.paragraph: Twenty-week review a week after the sixth and last chemotherapy cycle: blood counts, thyroid on pembrolizumab, tapering morphine, mood and her work. [S]

Mrs. Lovelace returns a week after her sixth and last cycle of carboplatin and paclitaxel; pembrolizumab continues every three weeks. She has had no bleeding. Her average pain is 2 of 10, and she has used a breakthrough dose only twice in the past month. She would like to take less morphine. The tingling in her toes is unchanged. She feels a little more tired than usual but has no cold intolerance, constipation beyond her usual, weight gain, or palpitations. Her mood is better and she is working on new mathematical notes most mornings. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-20; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well, alert; blood pressure 114/72, pulse 78, weight 54.4 kg
Reflexes normal; grade 1 sensory neuropathy at the toes

Bleeding between periods and after intercourse, with heavier periods, a watery blood-stained discharge and a constant pelvic ache, for about five months; average pain 7 of 10 despite her opium tincture; a friable cervical mass found on examination and biopsied; cause not yet established at intake
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented final illness; superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 74 fL, ferritin 5 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs
S — Synthetic modern finding anchored to her documented final illness.

Adenocarcinoma of the endocervix, usual (HPV-associated) type, HPV 18 positive, FIGO 2018 stage IVB: a 5.2 cm tumor with left parametrial invasion, metastases to left pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes, and bilateral lung metastases on MRI and PET-CT; PD-L1 combined positive score 5, mismatch repair proficient, HER2 1+; treated with palliative pelvic radiation for bleeding and carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab, with specialist palliative care from diagnosis
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit, anchored to her documented uterine cancer; the cervical site is a synthetic choice.
Cancer-related pelvic pain, nociceptive and visceral, from the cervical tumor and its left parametrial extension
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit.

Long-term prescribed opioid therapy: opium tincture for recurrent pelvic and abdominal pain for about two years, measured at times with a household spoon, converted at intake to measured oral morphine; no opioid use disorder on a DSM-5 assessment; naloxone supplied
S — Synthetic modern history anchored to her documented laudanum and opium; not a claim about her real dosing.

Drug-induced constipation from long-acting morphine and ondansetron, a week after the first chemotherapy cycle: no bowel movement for five days, with bloating and cramping but passing wind, without vomiting; no bowel obstruction on examination; potassium and calcium normal; resolved with laxatives
S — Synthetic adverse drug effect; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Metastatic cervical adenocarcinoma, after six cycles; on pembrolizumab (C53.0). Counts recovering: hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL, white cells 4.2, neutrophils 2.4, platelets 188; creatinine 0.71 mg/dL, ALT 24 U/L. TSH 7.8 mIU/L with a normal free T4 of 1.0 ng/dL: subclinical hypothyroidism, most likely immune-related thyroiditis from pembrolizumab, grade 1; under the ASCO guideline pembrolizumab continues and levothyroxine is not needed unless TSH rises above 10 or symptoms develop. [S]
Continue pembrolizumab every 3 weeks.
TSH and free T4 in six weeks under the standing order.
Restaging CT in about six weeks.
Influenza, COVID-19, second zoster and second hepatitis B vaccines today, between cycles.

Cancer-related pelvic pain, well controlled (G89.3). Average 2 of 10 with almost no breakthrough doses after radiation and the tumor's response; she wants less morphine, and a slow reduction is appropriate. [S]
Long-acting morphine 15 mg at night only for two weeks, then stop.
Keep oral morphine 5 mg as needed and acetaminophen.
Telephone check in one week for any return of pain or withdrawal symptoms.

Long-term opioid therapy, tapering (Z79.891). Safe use throughout; no signs of use disorder. [S]
Keep naloxone at home; return unused morphine to a pharmacy take-back.

Anemia (D50.0). Hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL after chemotherapy; no bleeding. [S]
Blood count with pembrolizumab cycles.
